wall.note: Centre line traced from the 1922 survey (sheet 137-NE-3); height and thickness from the sources. Gates not drawn.

events.title: A salt post
events.text: Under the Song dynasty a small military outpost here managed the salt trade.

facts.claim: A Song dynasty military outpost managed the salt trade here

events.title: Thirty guards
events.text: About thirty guards were stationed on the site.

facts.claim: About 30 guards were stationed at the site

events.title: A coastal fort
events.text: A small coastal fort was set up after Tung Lung Fort was abandoned.

facts.claim: A small coastal fort was set up after Tung Lung Fort was abandoned

events.title: The walled fort

photo.caption: Kowloon, Kwangtung province, China. Photograph by John Thomson, 1870.

events.text: After Britain took Hong Kong Island in 1842, the Qing government walled the fort and built the Yamen, the magistrate's office. The granite wall was about 4 m tall and 4.6 m thick, with four entrances. Its line here is traced from the 1922 survey.

facts.claim: The walled fort and Yamen were completed in response to British Hong Kong (Treaty of Nanking 1842)
The Qing wall was about 4 m tall and 4.6 m thick, with four entrances
The city wall's line traced on the 1922 survey
facts.value: about 660 m around, enclosing about 2.7 ha

events.title: Left out of the lease
events.text: The 1898 Convention leased the New Territories to Britain but excluded the walled city, then home to about 700 people. British forces took it in April 1899 and the Qing officials left; only about 150 residents remained.

facts.claim: The Convention for the Extension of Hong Kong Territory (9 Jun 1898) leased the New Territories but excluded the walled city
sources: This House (YouTube), 'The Densest City in Human History: A Rare Look Inside Kowloon Walled City', 28 Apr 2026, 12:20

facts.claim: Population when the 1898 Convention excluded the city
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18

facts.claim: British forces took the city on 14 Apr 1899; Qing officials left
After the British attack of 14 Apr 1899 only the mandarin and about 150 residents remained

events.title: The first survey

photo.caption: Rooftop scenery and city wall in the Kowloon Walled City

events.text: The Lands Department's 1922 survey draws the wall, the Yamen and a few streets of low houses inside: the earliest map in this model's time-lapse.

facts.claim: The city wall's line traced on the 1922 survey
facts.value: about 660 m around, enclosing about 2.7 ha

facts.claim: Features marked on the May 1987 survey: the H-shaped former Yamen labelled 'School', a clinic beside it, a temple on Tin Hau Temple Street, several shrines ('Shr'), wells ('W'), two public latrines ('Lat'), a footbridge ('FB'), an electric transformer ('ET') at the south edge, temporary structures ('TS') and a garden along the east side

events.title: The wall comes down
events.text: During the Japanese occupation the wall was pulled down and its stone used to extend Kai Tak airport.

facts.claim: The Japanese occupation force dismantled the wall and used the stone to extend Kai Tak airport
sources: House of Lords debate 'Walled City of Kowloon', HL Deb 11 June 1974 vol 352 cc463-76 (Lord Kennet, Earl Cowley, Lord Goronwy-Roberts)

events.title: Squatters and a fire
events.text: After the war about 2,000 squatters moved in. An attempt to clear them in January 1948 failed, and Britain adopted a hands-off policy. A fire in January 1950 destroyed over 2,500 huts in the area.

facts.claim: Squatters in the walled city
An attempt to clear squatters in January 1948 failed and Britain adopted a hands-off policy
sources: This House (YouTube), 'The Densest City in Human History: A Rare Look Inside Kowloon Walled City', 28 Apr 2026, 12:20

facts.claim: A January 1950 fire destroyed over 2,500 huts, home to nearly 3,500 families and 17,000 people

events.title: Low-rise growth
events.text: By the 1961 survey the old fort is packed with small buildings. A 1959 murder trial had ruled that Hong Kong had jurisdiction here, but the city stayed largely unpoliced.

facts.claim: A 1959 murder trial ruled that Hong Kong had jurisdiction in the city
Police entered only in large groups and made few raids

events.title: A clearance halted
events.text: A clearance attempt was halted after protests from Beijing. Residents formed a committee that became the kaifong association, which settled disputes and recorded property sales. One account says buildings were still only 1–2 storeys.

facts.claim: A clearance attempt was halted after protests from Beijing
sources: House of Lords debate 'Walled City of Kowloon', HL Deb 11 June 1974 vol 352 cc463-76 (Lord Kennet, Earl Cowley, Lord Goronwy-Roberts)

facts.claim: The kaifong association (from a 1963 anti-demolition committee) settled disputes and registered land titles outside the colony's courts
sources: J.L. Battenfeld, 'Walled City a place of myths and crime', UPI, 18 Dec 1984

facts.claim: In 1963 buildings were only 1-2 storeys and alleys were 8-10 ft of mud
sources: House of Lords debate 'Walled City of Kowloon', HL Deb 11 June 1974 vol 352 cc463-76 (Lord Kennet, Earl Cowley, Lord Goronwy-Roberts)

events.title: The towers rise; the raids

photo.caption: An aerial view of the Kowloon Walled City and the neighboring Sai Tau Tsuen village in 1973.

events.text: Aerial photos show towers rising across the city. In 1973–74 police made more than 3,500 raids and over 2,500 arrests, and triad power waned.

facts.claim: More than 3,500 police raids, over 2,500 arrests and over 1,800 kg of drugs seized; triad power waned afterwards
Municipal figure of 27,000 came from counting windows; officials privately put it at 45,000
sources: House of Lords debate 'Walled City of Kowloon', HL Deb 11 June 1974 vol 352 cc463-76 (Lord Kennet, Earl Cowley, Lord Goronwy-Roberts)

events.title: The height limit

photo.caption: The south side of the Kowloon Walled City in 1975. The elevation of the buildings begins to reach it's maximum height.

events.text: The authorities began enforcing the height limit set by the Kai Tak approach, at about 13–14 storeys; two buildings lost their top floors. From here the model shows the towers as surveyed in 1987.

facts.claim: Authorities began enforcing the height limit in 1975; two buildings lost their top floors
sources: J.L. Battenfeld, 'Walled City a place of myths and crime', UPI, 18 Dec 1984

facts.claim: A height limit of 13-14 storeys applied because of the Kai Tak approach
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18

events.title: The Joint Declaration
events.text: The Sino-British Joint Declaration set Hong Kong's return to China in 1997 and cleared the way for the city's demolition.

facts.claim: The Sino-British Joint Declaration set Hong Kong's 1997 return and laid the groundwork for demolition

events.title: The survey and the announcement
events.text: Police and Housing Department staff sealed the city and counted about 33,000 residents, and demolition was announced. The May 1987 survey sheet, which this model is traced from, is the last to map the city plot by plot.

facts.claim: On 14 Jan 1987 the demolition was announced; police and Housing Department staff sealed the city and surveyed every household
sources: HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember

facts.claim: The government survey of 14 Jan 1987 counted about 33,000 residents: the best anchor figure
Building plots outlined on the May 1987 sheet
facts.value: 482 building plots, 454 with a printed number (plus the Yamen halls, 4 temple plots, 2 latrines, a shrine)

events.title: The last years

photo.caption: An aerial photo of the Kowloon Walled City taken in 1989. The new park which was laid out at the site of the former Sai Tau Tsuen squatter settlement is visible at the south edge o

events.text: The 1989 survey sheet already leaves the city blank. Compensation of about HK$2.7 billion was paid to owners, tenants and businesses.

facts.claim: The 1989 edition of sheet 11-NE-11A leaves the city blank, labelled 'Kowloon Walled City', with no plots inside
Compensation totalled about HK$2.7 billion (US$350 million), roughly HK$82,000 per person

events.title: Eviction

photo.caption: Kowloon Walled City - Hong Kong - this was shortly before they demolished the place and replaced it with quite a nice park

events.text: The last residents were forcibly evicted between November 1991 and July 1992.

facts.claim: Holdouts were forcibly evicted between Nov 1991 and Jul 1992
sources: HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember
Robert Benjamin, 'Denizens of noted hellhole face Walled City eviction', Baltimore Sun, 30 Jun 1992

events.title: Demolition
events.text: The city was taken down by hand and machine rather than explosives, because of the airport next door. The model's order of demolition is illustrative.

facts.claim: Demolition ran from 23 Mar 1993 to Apr 1994, by hand and machine rather than explosives (near the airport)
sources: HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember

events.title: The South Gate found
events.text: Clearing the site uncovered the foundations of the South Gate and two granite plaques. With the Yamen they were declared monuments in 1996.

facts.claim: Surviving remnants: the Yamen (built 1847) and the South Gate foundations and two granite plaques ('South Gate', 'Kowloon Walled City') unearthed in 1994; both declared monuments on 4 Oct 1996

events.title: The park
events.text: Kowloon Walled City Park was completed in August 1995 and opened on 22 December. Its paths and pavilions are named after the city's streets and buildings. Trees in the model are illustrative.

facts.claim: Kowloon Walled City Park was completed in Aug 1995 and opened by Governor Chris Patten on 22 Dec 1995
The park's paths and pavilions are named after streets and buildings of the walled city

events.title: The Yamen remains
events.text: The Yamen still stands in the middle of the park, the only building of the walled city left.

facts.claim: Surviving remnants: the Yamen (built 1847) and the South Gate foundations and two granite plaques ('South Gate', 'Kowloon Walled City') unearthed in 1994; both declared monuments on 4 Oct 1996
Yamen hall footprints traced from the 2024 survey
facts.value: about 49 x 16 m overall; 6 roofed parts totalling about 490 m2
